objective: Implement TD-R001, TD-R002, TD-R003, TD-R004, TD-R008, TD-R016, and TD-R023
why: Harden update readiness and add encrypted/scheduled backups, automatic maintenance, security auditing, consolidated health, and centralized retention without expanding the browser command surface.
acceptance_criteria: Updater skips incomplete releases and selects the newest compatible package with a finalized SHA-256 digest.
Portable backups support password-based authenticated encryption and validate before publication or restore.
Administrators can configure scheduled backups with retention pruning.
Administrators can opt into automatic updates within a maintenance window with pre-update backup and existing rollback safeguards.
Security-sensitive history events are mirrored into a dedicated redacted audit store.
Administrators have a consolidated system-health view for dashboard, disk, backups, updates, clients, integrations, and audit status.
Retention centrally covers history, audit records, local backup count, and stale update artifacts.
Source/unit, UI/syntax, source-package, and Windows executable validation pass before release.
decisions: Keep dashboard.py stable and compose the milestone through a runtime process adapter.
Keep the in-app Recovery Console removed; new operational visibility is structured and administrator-only.
Automatic updates remain opt-in and run only inside an explicit local maintenance window.
Incomplete GitHub releases never displace the newest updater-ready release.
Audit payloads redact secret-looking fields before persistence.
out_of_scope: External backup destinations, MFA/SSO, API tokens, code signing, and destructive Recovery.exe actions.
next_action: Run the pull-request validation matrix, fix any integration failures, then prepare the next updater-visible prerelease.
